title: O Jesus, King Most Wonderful
description: O Jesus, King Most Wonderful in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Bernard of Clairvaux wrote these words in Latin. Edward Caswall's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 90.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Je-sus, King most won-der-ful, Thou Con-quer-or re-nowned, Thou Sweet-ness most in-ef-fa-ble, In whom all joys are found!

lines: In whom all joys are found!
When once Thou visitest the heart,
O Jesus, Light of all below,
Thou Fount of life and fire,
Surpassing all the joys we know,
May every heart confess Thy name,
To seek Thee more and more.
Thee may our tongues forever bless,
And ever in our lives express

licence: Public domain: Bernard of Clairvaux died in 1153; Edward Caswall died in 1878.
credits: Words by Bernard of Clairvaux (1090–1153), translated by Edward Caswall (1814–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
